title: Scott Wiener Says 2026 Tough for Progressive Jews Running for Congress
text:
California State Sen. Scott Wiener says 2026 is not an easy year for a progressive Jew running for Congress and calls out targeting of Jewish candidates and officials.
California State Sen. Scott Wiener, a Democratic U.S. House candidate, said on Thursday during an appearance on CNN's Inside Politics that 2026 is not an easy year for a progressive Jew running for Congress. He made the remarks while discussing the harassment and assault he experienced around the Trans March in San Francisco, saying the incident reflects a fringe perspective and does not represent the vast majority of march attendees.
Wiener told host Dana Bash that Jewish candidates and Jewish elected officials have been targeted in San Francisco and around the country and are held to a different standard than non-Jewish candidates with similar positions.
Context of the Trans March Incident
Wiener said the harassment and assault at or before the Trans March does not reflect the vast majority of people who attended the march. He said the incident reflects a very fringe perspective in terms of engaging in physical harassment of people.
He also said San Franciscans like him are horrified by what Israel has done in destroying Gaza and killing so many people, as well as its actions in the West Bank to push Palestinians out of their homes and communities.
Wiener stated that he believes Israel has committed genocide in Gaza, adding that regardless of what word someone chooses to use, people can disagree with him, but the situation is horrific and must stop. He noted there are 7 million Jews and 7 million Palestinians living in Israel, the West Bank and Gaza, and said no one is going anywhere and peace is needed.
He said the U.S. needs to be a force for peace and should not be funding destruction, which is why he does not support funding the Israeli military.
Targeting of Jewish Candidates
Dana Bash said that not funding the Israeli military is something that everybody Wiener is appealing to, and presumably the people who harassed him, also support. She noted it had been several months since the incident and asked whether he had any other thoughts about what their real goal was.
Wiener responded that 2026 is not, as he put it, an easy year to be a progressive Jew running for Congress. He said Jewish candidates and Jewish elected officials have been targeted in San Francisco and around the country and held to a different standard than non-Jewish candidates with similar positions.
He said it is an issue and that Jewish candidates and Jewish elected officials, not just him but others as well, have been getting targeted for several years, and that needs to stop.
Wiener said he has no problem being held accountable for anything he does or says or proposes or does not do or say, calling that democracy, and that he has hard conversations with his constituents all the time.
But he said when it rises to the level of straight-up harassment and intimidation and assault, that crosses a line, particularly when it is only targeting certain elected officials and candidates, specifically Jewish elected officials and candidates.
Political and Community Reactions
The comments came during a CNN Inside Politics interview that touched on both the personal incident and broader political tensions. Wiener is a California State Senator and a Democratic candidate for the U.S. House.
He described the targeting of Jewish candidates and officials as an ongoing problem that has persisted for several years and said it must stop.
He also emphasized that his criticism of Israel's actions does not excuse harassment or intimidation against Jewish candidates and elected officials, and that disagreements over policy should not cross into physical harassment or assault.
